nicknames: The Mecca of Canadian Harness Racing

main_track.bias_notes: Anti-clockwise. A premier 7/8-mile harness oval featuring broad, sweeping turns and a grueling 1,095-foot home stretch. NO PASSING LANE is present, meaning pocket-sitters (2nd along the rail) risk getting locked in if the front-runner tires. Outer-flow trips (1st-over and 2nd-over) are exceptionally potent.
main_track.post_bias: Posts 4, 5, and 6 are statistically dominant. Post 6 is designated as the 'Mohawk Sweet Spot' off the mobile gate wing. Post 1 carries a shuffle-back penalty for horses lacking early gate speed due to the absence of a sprint lane.

handicapping_angles.the_bullring_tax: Heavily downgrade horses shipping in from 1/2-mile regional bullrings (Flamboro Downs, Grand River, Western Fair, London). Half-mile specialists accustomed to short 400-foot stretches almost always run out of gas in Mohawk's 1,095-foot home lane.
handicapping_angles.pocket_trap_risk: Without a passing lane, beware of pocket sitters behind weak front-runners. Upgrade 1st-over (uncovered) and 2nd-over (cover-following) outer-flow stalkers who have a clear path down the stretch.
handicapping_angles.sub_27_final_quarter_standard: Pay strict attention to individual L1/4 (last quarter) split times. To win in upper condition races or Preferred ranks at Mohawk, a pacer must be capable of pacing an individual 26.x or 27.x final quarter off cover.
handicapping_angles.driver_choice_intent_premium: Driver intent is paramount. Heavily upgrade top-tier Mohawk pilots (James MacDonald, Louis-Philippe Roy, Doug McNair, Bob McClure) when taking over from out-of-town drivers or choosing one starter over another.
